title: G3: Soundness — an infinite relative chain implies non-SN(R/S)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Direction:** existence of an infinite relative chain $\Rightarrow \neg\mathrm{SN}(R/S)$ (task (1)'s $\Rightarrow$).

Given $s_i^\#\to t_i^\#$ with $\sigma$ and $t_i^\#\sigma\to_{R\cup S}^{*}s_{i+1}^\#\sigma$, build an actual infinite $\to_{R/S}$ derivation.

**What must be proved:**
- Each pair $s_i^\#\to t_i^\#$ comes from a rule $\ell\to r\in R$ with $t_i\trianglelefteq r$; un-mark and embed in a context to realize a genuine $\to_R$ step $s_i\sigma\to_R C_i[t_i\sigma]$.
- The connection $t_i^\#\sigma\to_{R\cup S}^{*}s_{i+1}^\#\sigma$ must back-translate to $\to_{R\cup S}^{*}$ on unmarked terms in the same context, preserving the position; prove marked steps correspond to unmarked steps (marking lemma).
- Conclude an infinite $\to_{R\cup S}$ derivation with infinitely many $\to_R$ steps, hence $\neg\mathrm{SN}(R/S)$.

Edge cases: collapsing rules in $S$ (root may change), duplicating rules; verify the position-tracking argument still holds.
